label: Golden-angle phyllotaxis
source_title: November 23 is Fibonacci Day! — Beaty Biodiversity Museum, University of British Columbia
interpretation: Idealized divergence between successive florets: 360/phi^2, phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2. Not every sunflower exactly realizes this angle. A projected polar gap is a different measurement; numerical coincidence does not establish phyllotaxis or growth mechanism.

label: Fivefold axis in icosahedral virus capsids
source_title: Origin of icosahedral symmetry in viruses
interpretation: 360/5 is a rotation about a fivefold axis in icosahedral symmetry. Many, not all, virus capsids have this symmetry. This is not a universal angle between capsid components; projected polar-gap agreement does not reconstruct a capsid or establish biology.

label: Fivefold quasicrystal / Penrose signature
interpretation: 360/5 is a fivefold angular signature. Quasicrystal order occurs in real alloys; Shechtman received the 2011 Chemistry Nobel. Not all quasicrystals are fivefold. This target is not a test of quasiperiodicity; sampled projections do not implement a Penrose cut-and-project construction.

label: Regular hexagon central vertex spacing
source_title: Columnar Jointing — U.S. National Park Service
interpretation: 360/6 is the central spacing of a regular hexagon's vertices. Honeycomb and many basalt columns show hexagonal patterns, but different mechanisms. Basalt fracture junctions use about 120 degrees, not this 60-degree convention; columns can have other side counts. Agreement is not evidence of optimal disk packing or natural cause.
